articles.title: Will Britain finally apologise for its role in the slave trade – and why is it so important?

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Former home secretary wins 86% support in a membership vote to stand in May 2028
James Cleverly has been chosen by the Conservatives as their candidate in the next London mayoral election, with the former cabinet minister saying he would stand up to “anti-London” Andy Burnham.
Cleverly, who stood down as shadow communities secretary in August to focus on his mayoral ambitions, was overwhelmingly chosen in a vote of London Tory members from a three-strong shortlist, winning 86% of the ballot.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Tories select James Cleverly as candidate for London mayor

articles.author: Andrew Pulver
articles.description:
Westminster joins wave of ‘job-stealing’ memes after the actor’s late success edging out the other contenders to be the new 007
Everybody is trying to get a piece of the Bond action: even the UK government.
In a post on its official Instagram account, the UK government promoted its youth jobs guarantee scheme, first announced in August, with a picture of Robert Pattinson as Bond with the joke caption: “Robert Pattinson to apply for all 90,000 jobs created for young people through Youth Employment Scheme.”
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Robert Pattinson to apply for 90,000 more jobs? UK government trolls James Bond actor

articles.author: Ben Quinn Political correspondent
articles.description:
Ex-minister Jess Phillips admits government does not have power to compel platforms to remove distressing content

UK politics live – latest updates

A new online safety act is likely to be needed to tackle convicted criminals such as Russell Brand using social media platforms to broadcast messages from prison, Labour MP Jess Phillips has said.
Just days after his conviction, Brand’s wife, Laura, broadcast a message from her husband to their 6.6 million YouTube subscribers, claiming he was not guilty of sexual offences for which he had been convicted by a jury. The video has had almost 850,000 views.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: New law ‘may be needed’ after Google rejects call to remove Russell Brand’s YouTube prison message

articles.author: Severin Carrell Scotland editor
articles.description:
Running for more than four weeks, 2027 festival features staging of play starring Ewan McGregor and Alan Cumming 
The Edinburgh international festival is to stage its longest season next year when it marks 80 years since its foundation in the aftermath of the second world war.
The festival will run for just over four weeks in August 2027, longer than its customary three weeks, and focus heavily on the role of the arts in unifying cultures and transcending conflict.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Edinburgh festival to mark 80-year anniversary with longest ever season

articles.author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
articles.description:
Modelling in draft of 10-year London plan threatens Sadiq Khan’s promises on improving air quality
Car use in London will rise by 10% over the next decade with cycling and walking falling as a proportion of trips, according to an official forecast by the city’s mayoralty, putting into doubt Sadiq Khan’s promises on air quality and the environment.
Based on projections in the draft version of the latest 10-year London plan, drawn up by the mayor’s office and Transport for London (TfL), road congestion from a growing population would slow buses down, while packed tube services might require stations to close regularly to ease numbers.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Car use in London forecast to rise by 10% in next decade

articles.author: Patrick Barkham
articles.description:
Scientists use lightweight tracker to map wading bird’s extraordinary migration from Norfolk to the Arctic and back
A bar-tailed godwit called Phil has completed a 6,800-mile journey from Norfolk to Siberia and back again, in the first mapping of the endurance feats of this long-distance migrant.
A wading bird not much larger than a pigeon, the bar-tailed godwit is known for making the longest recorded non-stop migratory flight of any bird, with populations that visit Britain spending summers breeding in the Arctic Circle before retreating to the unfrozen wetlands of Britain in winter.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Meet Phil, the bar-tailed godwit tracked on a 6,800-mile round trip to Siberia

articles.author: Presented by Annie Kelly with Jessica Elgot and David McAllister; produced by Eleanor Biggs, Alex Atack, Harriet Mogie and Brian McNamara; executive producer Sami Kent
articles.description:
Deputy political editor Jessica Elgot and influential MEP David McAllister on the prospect of the UK rejoining the European Union, before Friday’s UK-EU summit
On Friday, Andy Burnham will be in Brussels, to sign off a series of new deals between the UK and the EU.
The prime minister claims the deals – covering areas from food to youth mobility to carbon emissions – will boost UK GDP by £17bn.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Brejoin? Is Andy Burnham going to reverse Brexit? – podcast

articles.author: Jessica Elgot Deputy political editor
articles.description:
No 10 is confident the PM can make the case for closer EU ties, while others worry about leaving the campaign solely in his hands
The launch of a pro-Brexit campaign was one of the few genuine surprises this week in Westminster, even if the arguments were straight out of a familiar playbook.
The video launched on X over the weekend, with scenes of riots in France, champagne flowing in Brussels, and European politicians saying how desperate they were for Britain’s cash.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The leave campaign has been resurrected, so how should Burnham respond?

articles.author: Denis Campbell Health policy editor
articles.description:
Health secretary said programme would help about 566,000 vulnerable people in England by April
More than half a million of the most vulnerable people in England will be offered help from joint NHS and social care teams that will pave the way for the promised national care service, Yvette Cooper has announced.
Elderly people, care home residents, those with dementia and people near the end of their lives will receive assistance from the new programme.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘Neighbourhood support teams’ to pave way for national care service, Cooper announces

articles.author: Ian Sample Science editor
articles.description:
Scientists tell Commons exposure to colibactin in early life is potential driver of early-onset colorectal cancer
Exposure to a bacterial toxin in early life has emerged as a leading suspect in the rise of bowel cancer among those under 50, MPs have heard.
Cases of early-onset bowel cancer have doubled in many countries in the past two decades, and while rising obesity and a fall in physical activity are contributors, researchers believe other factors must also be involved.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bacterial toxin produced by E coli leading suspect in rise in bowel cancer among under-50s

articles.author: Sandra Laville Environment correspondent
articles.description:
Populations at lowest level on record with 45% of native breeding species in decline, environment watchdog says
The environment secretary, Angela Eagle, her ministers and Natural England are breaking the law by failing to intervene to slow the “deeply concerning” decline of Britain’s wild birds, the UK’s environment regulator has said.
New data shows that wild bird populations have dropped to their lowest level on record, with almost half – 45% – of 132 native breeding species in decline over a five-year period.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: UK government ‘breaking the law’ by not stopping decline of wild birds

articles.author: Tobi Thomas Health and inequalities correspondent
articles.description:
Trust apologises after findings on treatment of 20 brain tumour patients under oncologist who retired in 2023
Cancer patients were severely harmed after being given years of unnecessary chemotherapy treatment by an NHS trust, a report has found.
Some people were misdiagnosed and given inappropriate courses of treatment, while others were incorrectly told that if they stopped chemotherapy they would die, according to a Royal College of Physicians (RCP) report.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Cancer patients at NHS trust harmed by years of unnecessary chemotherapy, report finds

articles.author: Helena Horton
articles.description:
Animal welfare charities criticise ‘backwards step’ on foie gras, production of which has been banned in UK since 2007
Ministers will drop plans to ban foie gras imports into the UK in order to smooth a trade deal with the EU that will be announced this week.
As first reported by the Financial Times, the proposed ban will be officially dropped on Friday when the government announces its sanitary and phytosanitary (SPS) trade deal with the EU to reduce checks and paperwork on imports and exports of food and drink with the bloc.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Ministers to drop foie gras imports ban to help seal EU food trade deal

articles.author: Hilary Osborne Consumer and money editor
articles.description:
It is possible to switch to a better tariff and save money despite the forecast rise next year

Average energy bill in Great Britain predicted to rise to £2,166

The energy price cap in Great Britain looks likely to go up by 26% in January. But your bills might not have to rise by the same amount. If you are paying a tariff that matches the price cap you could save by switching to something lower. And if you do it now, you could make a substantial saving.
Providers are offering fixed tariffs that work out up to £407 below the estimated price cap, according to price comparison website uSwitch. It’s worth noting that it’s the price of the energy you use that is fixed, not your bill – so you will still be charged according to what you use.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Energy price cap rise: how to switch providers

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal; produced by George McDonagh, Ivor Manley , Harriet Mogie and Rudi Zygadlo; executive producer Eli Block
articles.description:
There are about a million young people across the country not in employment, education or training. Could Alan Milburn’s landmark report help change that? Richard Partington reports
The UK has one of the worst rates in Europe when it comes to youth unemployment. From the savage cuts to youth services during austerity, to the impacts of the pandemic and now the threat of AI to entry level jobs, young people across the country are feeling that the social contract is broken.
But now Alan Milburn, the 68-year-old New Labour veteran, has published a radical review urging the government to spend billions on a new deal for young people.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Can Labour end the youth unemployment crisis? – podcast

articles.description:
Alan Milburn has warned that the UK is at risk of losing a generation of young people without radical reform to tackle youth unemployment. Speaking at the launch of his report at Google's London headquarters, the former health secretary insisted 'half measures will not do' as he outlined proposals to get more young people into work that could save the government £200m a year


Alan Milburn says his plan to get young people into work will save only £200m a year

UK politics live – latest updates

Neet ideas: what’s in Milburn’s report?

 Continue reading...
articles.title: Alan Milburn says 'Great British promise' to young people is being broken – video

articles.author: Presented by Pippa Crerar and Kiran Stacey, produced by Nada Smiljanic and Annie La Vespa, music by Axel Kacoutié; the executive producer is Maz Ebtehaj
articles.description:
It is a big week for Andy Burnham as two of his big policy priorities enter the spotlight. On Tuesday, the Milburn review of welfare for under-25s is published, which could ignite old Labour tensions over benefit cuts.
Then, later this week, Burnham will be in Brussels for the UK-EU summit to discuss a potential new deal. But, as Pippa has signalled, cabinet ministers have told Burnham to put the brake on some of the discussions to ensure the government is not out of step with the public.
Is it too little too late?
You can read Rowena Mason’s article on benefits for under-25s here.
You can watch episodes of Politics Weekly on our YouTube channel here.
Send your questions to Pippa and Kiran on politicsweeklyuk@theguardian.com
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Will Burnham put a ‘brake’ on push to rejoin EU? – podcast

articles.author: Presented by Nosheen Iqbal with Maeve McClenaghan . Video produced by James Tindale & Eleanor Biggs . Sound design by Eli Block . Motion graphics by Natalie Gegan . Executive produced by Homa Khaleeli, Elizabeth Cassin, Phil Maynard & Rachel Oldroyd
articles.description:
Multiple women allege David Walliams abused his power and position as a celebrity to prey on them for sexual purposes when they were young women, an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News has found. He denies the allegations.

In a letter addressed to journalists working on this investigation, Walliams writes: 'Looking back, I realise that at times I behaved thoughtlessly towards other people I had casual sexual relationships with.

'I realise I did not always take people’s feelings properly into account. That is something I regret. And whilst a power imbalance is inevitable when one party is famous, abusing that power is something else entirely and it is something that I never did.'

He adds: 'I am not a sexual predator. I have not broken the law, but I am devastated that some of the women I met 10 to 20 years ago have now expressed hurt or anger towards me.'
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The allegations against David Walliams | Investigation by the Guardian and ITV News

articles.author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
articles.description:
Residents of Astley in Greater Manchester will tell public inquiry next week of ‘cacophony’ of noise causing sleep deprivation and depression
When Stephen Retford retired from the police in 2006, he looked forward to a quiet life after nearly three decades catching villains. But now the former detective has landed another big case – one that is extremely close to home.
“It’s the total injustice of it,” the 70-year-old seethed, staring up at the 18-metre-high mega-warehouse that looms over the quiet village of Astley in Greater Manchester. Residents are up in arms about the “monster” construction, likening it to having a “cruise ship in our back garden”.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘It’s a feeling of being screwed over’: once-quiet village despairs over ‘monster’ warehouse

articles.author: Rory Carroll Ireland correspondent
articles.description:
Scheme in Derry aims to sow confidence by getting people with learning and physical disabilities into wrestling
The music thumped, the lights blazed and from the ring the announcer did a countdown. “Who is ready to rumble?” he roared. The bellows and cheers indicated that the crowd at St Columb’s Hall in Derry on Saturday night was more than ready for the Foyle Rumble, and so began a wrestling extravaganza of heroes and villains in leotards, masks and kneepads.
The blend of athleticism and scripted storytelling would have been familiar to fans of WrestleMania, but this Northern Irish version came with a twist: many of the performers have learning or physical disabilities, and the characters they play in the ring do not quite stay in the ring.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘No matter what, he doesn’t quit’: disabled wrestlers draw strength from ring alter egos

articles.author: Chris Osuh, Aamna Mohdin and Diane Taylor
articles.description:
Some relatives of British citizens say they feel left behind, but announcement has brought relief to many care workers
“The only time we’re regarded as human beings is when they need a lot of hands onboard, like during Covid. But after that, we’re tossed away like we’re some rubbish,” Aneisha Williams says.
Williams, 39, was months from qualifying for indefinite leave to remain after 10 years in the UK. But claiming housing benefit could delay her settlement for years under Shabana Mahmood’s “earned settlement” plans.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: ‘I feel free now’: Shabana Mahmood’s immigration shake-up provokes mixed emotions

articles.author: Sarah Hanson-Young
articles.description:
If the government bends to AI companies, artists, creatives and journalists will be the sacrificial lamb – and Australia will become a global pariah

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Right now, the prime minister faces a choice. Does he stand with Jimmy Barnes and the Working Class Man or does he stand with Big AI?
This week, some of the biggest names in Australian music, publishing, journalism and art have thrown down the gauntlet to the government. From Paul Kelly to Anna Funder and Peter Garrett, household names and Australian icons are all singing from the same song sheet.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Big tech is already building datacentres in Australia. Why is Labor so desperate to give them loopholes?

articles.author: Johana Bhuiyan
articles.description:
AI startup and Claude chatbot maker became one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded businesses with final share price of $97

Anthropic’s historic stock market debut: key takeaways, and what comes next for the AI industry 

Anthropic closed its first day of trading on the US stock market about 17% higher than its initial public offering price. At the close of market on Thursday, Anthropic shares were trading at just over $97 with a nearly $1.3tn total market capitalization, $1.75tn fully diluted.
While the final share value was higher than the IPO price of $83, it marked a dip from an early high of $111.50. The firm’s shares initially soared 34% when trading got under way on its US market debut on Thursday, valuing the company at more than $2tn. Nonetheless, Anthropic’s ranked among the biggest stock market flotations in history. The artificial intelligence startup, founded in 2021, became one of the most valuable publicly traded businesses in the world.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anthropic closes first day of public trading at $1.3tn valuation after largest-ever IPO

articles.author: Auzzy Byrdsell in New York and Lisa Bonos in San Francisco
articles.description:
Anti-AI groups gather in front of Nasdaq exchange in Times Square and Anthropic’s headquarters in San Francisco
As the artificial intelligence startup Anthropic debuted on the US stock market at an eye-popping $2tn valuation on Thursday, protesters from anti-AI groups rallied in front of the Nasdaq exchange at its New York City headquarters in Times Square and several were arrested. Similar demonstrations took place outside Anthropic’s San Francisco headquarters.
“I think people are starting to get that there’s something wrong,” Jose Gonzalez, 46, one of roughly 30 protesters in New York City, said. Protesters carried flags reading “STOP TECH OLIGARCHS” and “FREEZE AI: END ICE, END WAR”.

articles.title: Protesters rally against Anthropic in New York and San Francisco after $2tn stock market debut

articles.author: Nadeem Badshah
articles.description:
Hotly anticipated Bonnie and Clyde-inspired adventure GTA VI has gamers glued to their screens around the world
Grand Theft Auto fans around the world pulled all-nighters, skipped work and school, and attended overnight launch parties to vicariously embark on police chases and coordinate robberies as the latest instalment of the eagerly anticipated series arrived.
GTA VI, a Bonnie and Clyde-inspired crime adventure game set in the fictional US state of Leonida, was launched at midnight on Wednesday after a 13-year wait.

articles.title: Grand Theft Auto fans skip work and pull all-nighters to play new instalment

articles.author: Dan Milmo and Aisha Down
articles.description:
The company counts physicists, a former journalist and an associate of the pope among its guiding lights
The paper fortunes of Anthropic’s seven co-founders reached a total of more than $180bn on Thursday as shares in their company started trading at a price ahead of expectations.
The opening price of $111.50 (£85) per share valued the entrepreneurs’ stakes – including the chief executive, Dario Amodei, and his sister Daniela – at between $26.5bn and $27bn each. articles.title: Who are Anthropic’s seven co-founders, now worth $180bn?

articles.author: Nils Pratley
articles.description:
Can the newly listed AI company really be worth $2tn? Anyone who remembers the late 1990s has good reason to ask
Roll up, roll up, who wants to buy shares in a company whose technology “could pose catastrophic or existential risks to humanity”, as the prospectus had it? Virtually everybody, as it turned out. Anthropic flew out of the blocks on its first day as a listed company.
From the point of view of the promoters, the result was as good as it gets. The final pricing for the shares at $83 apiece was meaningfully higher than the indicated range of $70 to $78, but still left room for a big initial “pop”. There were positive vibes all round – especially for the battalion of investment banks collecting $550m of underwriting fees.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Anthropic keeps the AI party swinging, but the atmosphere is bubbly | Nils Pratley

Anthropic's CEO, Dario Amodei, issued a warning about the dangers of AI, saying it has 'very real' but 'avoidable' risks, shortly before the company rang the opening bell at Nasdaq

Anthropic ‘to open up more than 20% higher at over $100 a share’ after blockbuster IPO – business live

articles.title: Anthropic CEO acknowledges AI has 'very real risks' shortly before IPO – video

articles.author: Richard Partington and Kalyeena Makortoff
articles.description:
Kristalina Georgieva says countries needed to be ready for tech rollout, adding: ‘You snooze, you lose’

Business live – latest updates

Booming demand for artificial intelligence will force the world’s most powerful central banks to raise interest rates, the head of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) has warned.
Kristalina Georgieva, the managing director of the Washington-based fund, said demand for AI hardware and related technology products was pushing up consumer prices around the world.

articles.title: AI demand will push up interest rates around the world, IMF head warns

articles.author: Josh Taylor Technology reporter

A network of grassroots campaigners around the country is sharing information to help push back against the development boom

Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

When Heather Champion raised a council motion in March opposing a massive new gas plant to power a large datacentre in the southern highlands of New South Wales, it failed to pass.
Five months later, when the local councillor for Wingecaribee raised a new motion calling for the federal government to implement a moratorium on new datacentres, it passed unanimously.

articles.title: ‘Communities are really angry’: how Australia’s datacentre opposition has gone from marginal to mainstream in five months

articles.author: Keza MacDonald
articles.description:
Rockstar Games’ brilliant 18-rated criminal caper is stuffed with sex, drugs and violence. It is the most explicit game I’ve ever played – and it really is not for kids

Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

I am haunted still by an interaction I had at my stepson’s ninth birthday party in 2014, where one of the kids asked if I could put on Grand Theft Auto V for them all. “I have it at home!”, he said, giving me the puppy-dog eyes. Mentally replaying that game in my head, flashing back to the many scenes involving such things as smoking meth, over-the-top gratuitous violence and grubby sex in one character’s trailer, I said “no way”. Later I gently mentioned to the kid’s mother that GTA V was an 18-rated game and really wasn’t suitable for kids. “Oh, but he’s really good at these games,” she told me. She was genuinely shocked to learn that an 18-rating on a video game was a flag for adult content, rather than an indication of its difficulty.
Grand Theft Auto VI is released this week. It is an incredible creative and technical feat, conjuring a realistic-looking and exhaustively detailed virtual Florida filled with every kind of filth and criminality you could imagine. It is brilliant, entertainingly observed and even sometimes unexpectedly touching, largely thanks to a central love story between the player couple, Jason and Lucia. It is lewd, violent and frequently hilarious. It is also absolutely full of stuff that I really would not want my 10 and seven-year-old boys to see or hear. I have never played a game that has more thoroughly earned its 18 rating.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Parents: please don’t buy Grand Theft Auto VI for your child

articles.author: Lauren Almeida
articles.description:
CEO of Cambridge-based firm viewed as leading contender to replace co-founder Jensen Huang according to reports

Business live – latest updates

Nvidia’s headhunters have reportedly approached the chief executive of the Cambridge-based chip company Arm, in its search for a new leader after Jensen Huang’s dramatic exit.
Heidrick & Struggles, the recruiting firm hired by the company’s board, has started contacting potential candidates, according to Bloomberg.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Nvidia approaches Arm boss Rene Haas in search for new CEO

articles.author: Keza MacDonald
articles.description:
There’s a vast amount to absorb in Leonida, but these pointers will rev up your criminal engines and allow you to better enjoy the ride

Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

Leonida is so huge as to be overwhelming and in the opening hours, the game bombards you with tonnes of info that you will inevitably forget. But I’ve done nothing but play this game for weeks and I’m here to help. Here’s what I wished I’d known at the start
Walk faster. I found that Jason and Lucia walk incredibly slowly. If you go into the options menu, you can select “fast walk” as the default walking speed, which sped them up just a little without ruining the pace or atmosphere of the game. While you’re in there, you can also customise plenty of other things, including controls and button mapping.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Bank your stolen cash, bring a change of clothes, go easy on the bloodshed: 15 tips for playing Grand Theft Auto VI

articles.author: Jared Beasley
articles.description:
A professional sports career does not guarantee wealth. And a growing number of athletes are turning to alternative streams of income
“I’m sick and tired of it.” Bart Swings tossed his jacket behind him. It was August 2025, the Winter Olympics were less than six months away, and the Belgian Olympic champion’s injured knee was not getting better. The clip, profanity and all, later ran on the Belgian evening news along with the weather and the football. But the injury update didn’t come from an interview – it was broadcast on the speed skater’s OnlyFans channel.
The subscription site, best known for porn dudes, cam girls and dubiously horny couples, has quietly assembled one of the stranger rosters in professional sport. The list, about 285 athletes deep, includes Olympic speed skaters and rowers, tennis players, surfers and golfers. And, despite its racy reputation, many of the athletes on OnlyFans are not putting out adult content.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: From training clips to thirst traps: why athletes are turning to OnlyFans

articles.author: Hosted and produced by Matilda Boseley
articles.description:
Grand Theft Auto has been so central to the moral panic over graphic video games that some experts have called it the "grand theft fallacy". Yet the outrage was originally seeded by the studio itself in 1997 to drum up hype and taboo curiosity for its clunky-looking debut. Nearly 30 years on, that engineered scandal is still bearing fruit. 


Grand Theft Auto VI review – gaming’s most depraved world is now also its greatest love story

articles.title: How GTA started its own moral panic – video

articles.author: Nadia Khomami Arts and culture correspondent
articles.description:
Reviewers praise relationship between two leads in hotly anticipated release, whose trailer attracted 90m views in 24 hours

Tell us: are you playing Grand Theft Auto VI?

Good things clearly come to those who wait. After 13 years of anticipation, Grand Theft Auto VI is finally here – and, according to critics, it’s a masterpiece.
The trailer for the video game, which returns players to Vice City, Rockstar’s fictional version of Miami, attracted more than 90m views in 24 hours when it was released in December 2023. Excitement continued to mount, with two release delays and a steady stream of leaks and speculation keeping the game in the headlines.

articles.title: ‘Most extraordinary virtual world’: critics hail Grand Theft Auto VI as masterpiece

articles.author: Associated Press
articles.description:
The autonomous driving company suspended driverless taxi rides on US highways days after California banned the vehicles on its own freeways
Waymo has stopped offering driverless taxi rides on freeways across the US indefinitely. The Alphabet subsidiary pulled its vehicles from highways nationwide after California banned them from freeways in response to recent traffic incidents.
Waymo had allowed riders to hail its robotaxis for freeway rides in the San Francisco Bay Area, Los Angeles, Phoenix, Miami and Austin. The California-based company offers rides on city streets in many other areas, including Las Vegas, Dallas and Denver. Those rides remain unaffected by suspended freeway service.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Waymo pulls driverless taxis from freeways across the US after California ban

articles.author: Steve May
articles.description:
Not sure which TV is right for you? Whether you want an affordable mini LED or a feature-packed OLED, here’s what our square-eyed expert recommends
• Do you really need to buy a new TV? How to upgrade your setup

If your TV looks like an off-cut from Stonehenge, isn’t quite as smart as your microwave or, heaven forfend, is boring old HD rather than 4K HDR (high dynamic range), it could be time to invest in something more up to date.
But even a cursory look at the latest TVs available will confirm a bewildering array of options, from super-slim models with unfeasibly large screens to high performers that rival the picture quality at your local cinema.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: The best TVs in the UK for every home and screen size, tested

articles.author: Johana Bhuiyan
articles.description:
Exclusive: three Senate Democrats send letters to tech CEOs saying safeguards against nudification apps are insufficient on their platforms
A trio of US senators says Apple and Google are failing to effectively detect or remove apps meant to generate nonconsensual nude or pornographic imagery. The senators also say Meta is continuing to profit off of ads for these so-called nudification apps that “victimize women and girls worldwide”.
On Wednesday, Ron Wyden, Ed Markey and Ben Luján sent letters to the CEOs of the tech companies, saying the safeguards they have in place to keep nudification off their app stores or platforms are not sufficient.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Senators criticize Apple and Google for letting teens access ‘nudify’ apps despite parental controls

articles.author: Andrew Lawrence
articles.description:
After refusing to obey the president’s Lake Ontario order, MapQuest briefly rose to No 1 in navigation apps. It’s now a tool in the US anti-surveillance movement
I am among the legion of former PC desk occupants with warm memories of MapQuest, the Y2K-era travel website that kept millennial drivers on course with sheaves of printed-out directions – a quantum leap over the ungainly glovebox map. But I assumed it had long since gone the way of AIM and Skype, its manual turn-by-turn guidance made obsolete by big tech.
Proof of life came in January 2025, when Donald Trump issued an executive order renaming the Gulf of Mexico the Gulf of America – a change Apple Maps and Google Maps promptly adopted, while MapQuest … did nothing. Not only had it never signed off, MapQuest was reinventing itself as a plucky oppositional hero, the app most likely to uphold your geographical beliefs.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: Annoying Trump and dodging Flock: inside MapQuest’s contrarian comeback

articles.author: Nicola Davis Science correspondent
articles.description:
Research to look at whether ban can make meaningful change in mental health and wellbeing for under-16s
Countries around the world are considering social media bans for children, but whether this would work in practice has been hotly debated. Now researchers are seeking answers through a major scientific study led by Wellcome, which will be the first of its kind.
Ten research projects will explore topics ranging from children’s mental health to their sleep and physical activity, comparing factors before and after the social media ban for children under 16 is introduced in the UK in spring 2027.
 Continue reading...
articles.title: £10m ‘once-in-a-generation’ study to explore effects of children’s social media ban

articles.author: Anna Betts and Blake Montgomery
articles.description:
Google’s Gmail also affected after problems reported in technological infrastructure in the US and worldwide
Thousands reported disruptions to Google’s Gmail and Apple’s iPhone apps, such as Apple Pay and iCloud, on Tuesday, according to Downdetector. Apple confirmed the outages in a statement but said it had resolved them, while Google said it had not seen internal signs of outages.

articles.author: Michael Savage Media editor
articles.description:
Agreement secured by Equity union gives actors rights over payment and consent when digital replicas are used
Actors in the UK are to be given more rights over their “digital replicas” as part of a new agreement on AI protections with TV and film producers, secured after a growing on-set backlash.
Under a wide-ranging new deal secured by Equity, the actors’ union, performers will have the rights to be paid when their digital replicas are used and to consent to whether their digital replica is used or not.

CEO’s affair and resignation has brought company’s murky corporate contracts and supply chains into sharp focus
